name: Ferrari World Yas Island, Abu Dhabi
review_text:
Ferrari World Abu Dhabi is a dream destination for speed junkies and automotive enthusiasts alike. One of the best parts of the experience is that the entire park is indoors, providing a comfortable, climate-controlled environment to enjoy world-class thrills regardless of the weather outside.

The absolute standout ride is Formula Rossa. As the fastest roller coaster in the world, its lightning-fast acceleration is something you have to feel to believe; it is truly the ultimate adrenaline rush.

For those seeking sheer intensity, Flying Aces is incredibly thrilling, featuring one of the world's highest roller coaster loops.

I also highly recommend Mission Ferrari, which stands out as a brilliantly interactive and immersive roller coaster that blends physical drops with high-tech storytelling.

Even the Turbo track provides a great ride, adding to the variety of the park.

Beyond the heart-pounding attractions, the atmosphere is elevated by the stunning display of Ferrari car models. Seeing the evolution and craftsmanship of these iconic machines up close makes the visit all the more impressive. Whether you are there for the record-breaking speeds or the Italian luxury, Ferrari World is a top-tier attraction that shouldn't be missed.

review_text:
Extremely Disappointing Experience – Total Waste of Money

I had one of the worst theme park experiences of my life at Ferrari World Abu Dhabi, and I strongly regret coming here.

I visited with my family who came all the way to Dubai to see me, including my young siblings who were extremely excited about Ferrari World. I spent over 2,200 AED just on tickets, expecting a world-class experience. What no one tells you — and what should be clearly mentioned — is that waiting times are absolutely insane: 2 to 5 HOURS per ride.

When we arrived, all fast pass tickets were already sold out. I went to the information desk and politely asked if they could help us with just TWO fast pass tickets for my young siblings, explaining that they might never get the chance to visit again. The answer was a flat NO, no empathy, no effort to help, nothing.

As a result, we managed to ride only ONE roller coaster after waiting 2.5 hours. When we tried to go to other rides, the queues were 3 to 4 hours long. This is completely unacceptable and honestly insane for a paid attraction at this price level.

My younger siblings were heartbroken and disappointed, and as a family we felt cheated. This place is severely overcrowded, clearly with no limit on the number of people allowed inside, and the management seems to care only about selling tickets, not about visitor experience.

Unless you buy fast pass tickets WELL IN ADVANCE, do NOT come here. Otherwise, you will spend your entire day standing in lines and walking around doing nothing.

Ironically, the best time to visit is probably summer, because right now it feels like they are just taking people’s money for nothing. For the price paid, this experience was absolutely not worth it.

I do NOT recommend Ferrari World to anyone without fast pass tickets. Save your money or go somewhere that actually values its guests.

name: Warner Bros. World™ Yas Island, Abu Dhabi
review_text:
I am a theme-park enthusiast and I’ve traveled visiting many parks and resorts all over the world.

What I found at Warner Bros World just blew me away! Although I had done my homework and studied the park in advance (reading thru the website and watching vlogging YouTube videos) I was still shocked by the high-level quality of experience this park offered!

My son and I visited on New Year’s Eve and although we were told the park would be really busy because of the holidays — it was still a very manageable experience… nothing compared to a busy day at Disneyland 🤣

The first two hours of the day were the least busiest… a good time to visit the more popular attractions (Batman: Knight Flight and Tom & Jerry’s Spin)

But throughout the day we were able to enjoy ourselves at a good and simple pace… some rides… popcorn… character interactions (…and I mean intentional interactions, not just photos!)… strolling through the park taking photos (beautiful and detailed scenery throughout the whole place)… ribeye steak lunch in Bedrock… show in the main hall area… such an amazing time.

I have to say… Warner Bros World in Abu Dhabi is one of the best! And I’ll tell you why:

1. Excellent and Friendly Employees!!! I know this should be a given when dealing with the service industry… but more and more many theme parks are beginning to lower their standards in this area. However, I found every single employee at WB World to be so absolutely friendly, helpful and excellent in their area of service. While shopping in the Bedrock Boutique, two employees: Pride and Bushra, gave me FIRST CLASS shopping experience… walking me through the store and helping me to find everything Flintstone that I wanted (I’m a huge Fred Flintstone fan!)… big friendly smiles and wonderful conversations about the local area and culture. These friendly employees really make a difference in making you feel welcomed and in having such an enjoyable day in the park!

2. Character Interactions. Not only can you meet and get a photo with the characters, but they actually take time to interact with you. For example, Robin and Batwomen took no less than 5 minutes talking to us, asking us questions, making funny jokes and just making our experience so much more fun! They were amazing! Later on, we met the Flintstones and although they can’t talk, they made motions and communicated in creative ways… again, interacting and making the whole experience so much more than just taking a photo. It’s a higher level of theming altogether. Just amazing.

3. Awesome rides and attractions! I’ve visited Warner Bros Movie World in Australia (and I love it there!) but the rides and attractions at this Warner Bros World are so much more different and highly themed. I kept telling my son “these rides are so world-class” — they could easily compete alongside anything at Disney. Creative and fun… just loved them all! My favorite was the Bedrock River Adventure, but that’s because I’m a huge Flintstones fan! Love what they did with them here… and I hope they’ll never get rid of this area. I grew up in the years when Hanna-Barbera cartoons were the main programs we watched on Saturday morning television… it’s so nostalgic to see these cartoons coming back to life here at this park. Cartoon Junction was also another favorite area with Tom & Jerry, Scooby Doo and the Looney Tunes! My son (in his twenties) really loved the Metropolis and Gotham areas and attractions in this park.

Also notable mentions for the delicious food selections and many places to sit and relax in the park. Worldclass attraction that should be visited by anyone looking to have a fun day at a theme park. Loved it so much!

review_text:
We liked this place overall.

The thing that bummed us the most about this place was the staff's behavior at the entry gate. They were checking bags and the checking lady in the extreme right line was super rude. She not only made us throw all food we had, but also spoke in a very condescending tone and humiliated us out of the queue.

I requested her to let us keep a piece of cake we got for our son, but NO, she asked us to throw that too. How else would food vendors inside the park earn if we get our son's favorite cake inside the park, even if it were to make sure he's not famished in the first half of the day.

I am all in for compliance and following rules, just be a little flexible when it comes to kids and a small piece of cake ain't hurting anybody. Toddlers are hard to console when something they're looking forward to, gets thrown in the bin.

Nevertheless, we started with the dolphin show. Very average. Kudos to the dolphins, but the stage presenters really need to up their game. No one could understand a word they said. The dolphin show at the Dubai Dolphinarium was wayyyyyyyyy better. Also, what's with the reserved seating at the auditorium ? You wouldn't give reserved seats to folks with toddlers even if they reach the auditorium well before the show, but quick pass owners get reserved seating even at the last minute? I understand quick pass folks getting quick access , but why give them reserved seating ?

Anyway, endless ocean and Arctic circle is beautifully maintained at Sea World. We loved the penguin area and how everybody gets a chance to get close to the penguins in a habitat that suits them.

Loved the Polar region too, the Walrus was the big showstopper at the park. Maybe do something about the stench in that area ?

Food at Seaworld is pretty expensive, but the café near the penguin area is particularly goood and has good value for money.

We missed the mermaid show and there was just 1 show in the entire day. It was a bummer to not have caught that show. Felt like there could be announcements in the park or displays that showed timings and venues to these things..

The amazing 360 displays at the center of the park enthrall you and present a spectacular view of the shows.

We kept checking with various staff members about the "Pick a pearl" bit, but we failed to get any clarity on what it was all about and left without taking that experience ultimately.

Seaworld does seem promising for a future visit. I'd like to give it another go in the future, hoping for a much better experience next time 🤞

review_text:
Major safety failure: no staff or security response to threats during a family show

We attended a show here with our two children (aged 4 and 7). What happened raised serious concerns about guest safety and the venue’s ability to manage incidents inside the amphitheater.

Seating was unassigned and guests were taking any available seats. I entered first and seated our child in a single free seat. No one indicated that the seat was reserved or being held. When my husband arrived a few minutes later, he sat with our child (the child remained in the same seat, sitting on his lap). At that point, a nearby group suddenly claimed the seat was being held.

A man from that group arrived about a minute before the end of the show and immediately began shouting at my husband, claiming the seat and making direct physical threats, all while standing next to our child. The situation continued despite the show being almost finished.

Most concerning was the complete lack of response from the venue. There was no visible staff or security presence in the amphitheater, and no intervention at any point. I was forced to leave one of our children alone and go into the corridor to try to find help, yet no assistance came. Even after the show ended, the aggressive behaviour continued and we left feeling unsafe.

The impact on our family was significant. Our children were frightened and distressed, and the rest of our day was affected by stress and anxiety after what should have been a normal family outing.

When we approached reception ourselves, we were told to stand in a queue and submit a complaint. This is not an appropriate response when guests have been threatened and children are involved. Later, we received an official reply describing the incident as a “misunderstanding.” We strongly disagree: physical threats, lack of intervention, and distressed children are not a misunderstanding.

We expect a formal follow-up from management and clear action to ensure visible staff and security presence, proper escalation procedures, and active monitoring during family shows. Without these measures, families cannot feel safe attending events at this venue.

We were extremely disappointed upon arriving at Waterworld to purchase tickets for ourselves and our family visiting from overseas. We had received an email confirming that a discount would be valid until a specific date, as clearly stated in the message. However, when we arrived, we were informed that the original dates had been changed and that the discount no longer applied. As a result, we were required to pay full price for our family of six.

Unfortunately, this meant the cost was more than double what we had planned for, and we had to inform our family that we could no longer go — despite everyone already being packed, dressed, and excited for the day. This experience was extremely upsetting and left us feeling very disappointed.

Your feedback is important to us, and we regret the inconvenience caused. Please share your details to feedback@yasconcierge.com so we can review this matter further and assist you accordingly.
